newsitem.title: USA: Merck backs 97 EPS estimate range.
newsitem.headline: Merck backs 97 EPS estimate range.

text.p: Merck and Co Inc chief executive Raymond Gilmartin said on Wednesday he was comfortable with analysts' forecasts for the company's 1997 earnings per share in a $3.73-to-$3.85 range.
Gilmartin told shareholders at the company's annual meeting here that he had indicated to industry analysts that "I'm comfortable with that range."
Merck earned $3.20 a share in 1996 after $2.70 in 1995.
Responding to a shareholder question, Gilmartin said the pharmaceutical giant was not planning to split its stock in the near future.
"We have no immediate plans for a stock split at this point," he said.
Merck's shares closed on Wednesday down 1-1/2 at 87-3/4.
Gilmartin said he expected the company's Zocor cholesterol-lowering drug to continue to be a high-growth drug, despite increasing competition.
"The cholesterol-lowering market is a high-growth market," Gilmartin said. He said he expected Zocor to compete well against other cholesterol-lowering drugs.
Earlier this month, Merck's shares sold off amid investor concern over strong initial sales from Warner-Lambert Co's cholesterol-lowering drug Lipitor.
Zocor had worldwide sales of $2.8 billion in 1996.
Gilmartin reiterated earlier statements that Merck expects to spend $1.7 billion in 1997 on research and development. "I think we're spending appropriately" on R&D, he said.
The Merck CEO said the company's pipeline of new drugs and the expanding global pharmaceutical market would allow for sufficent growth without needing a major acquisition.
"I see no need to engage in alliances, acquisitions or mergers to protect earnings per share growth," he said.
